article_title: TU Wien Physicists Detect Record-Deep Quantum Entanglement in a Centimeter-Sized Strange-Metal Crystal
summary: Approvable News piece with a solidly-sourced headline/summary/lead; manual review found a misattributed quote and two unverifiable body-paragraph figures, each recoverable via a corrections record.

findings.message: Source fetched via Archive.org fallback (original returned 200)
Quote misattributed to the wrong cited outlet
findings.details: The body quotes: 'quantifies how sensitively a quantum system responds to a change,' citing Physics World. Physics World's own snapshot (source-1.html.gz) does not contain this as a direct quote — it paraphrases QFI as 'roughly, a measure of how sensitively a quantum state depends on a given parameter.' The exact verbatim phrase actually appears as a direct quote from Silke Bühler-Paschen in the phys.org snapshot (source-2.html.gz: '"The quantum Fisher information quantifies how sensitively a quantum system responds to a change," explains Bühler-Paschen.') and is repeated in The Quantum Insider (source-4.html.gz). The quote itself is real and verbatim, but attributed to the wrong outlet and left unattributed to its actual speaker.

findings.message: Two specific technical figures are not present in the cited snapshot content
findings.details: (1) 'energy resolution of about 0.07 meV' is cited to phys.org and the arXiv paper; neither source-2.html.gz (phys.org) nor source-5.html.gz (arxiv.org/abs page) contains '0.07' or 'meV' anywhere in the captured text. (2) 'the QFI witness reached a value of 8.2, which the authors call "the very most conservative estimate"' is cited solely to the arXiv paper; source-5.html.gz is the arXiv *abstract* page (title/authors/abstract only, 4,702 characters of extracted text) and contains neither '8.2' nor 'conservative' nor any numeric QFI witness value. These figures may well be accurate content from the full Nature Physics paper or full-text PDF, but the specific URL cited (the arXiv abstract page) and its captured snapshot do not substantiate them.

content_preview.title: TU Wien Physicists Detect Record-Deep Quantum Entanglement in a Centimeter-Sized Strange-Metal Crystal
content_preview.summary: Neutron-scattering measurements at ILL Grenoble found signs that at least nine particles are quantum-entangled at once inside a centimeter-sized strange-metal crystal, the deepest entanglement reported in any quantum material.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Physicists led by a team at TU Wien have found evidence of what may be the deepest quantum entanglement yet recorded in any material: a signal indicating that groups of at least nine particles act as a single entangled unit inside a strange-metal crystal large enough to hold in one hand. The measurements, taken on the ThALES cold-neutron spectrometer at the Institut Laue-Langevin (ILL) in Grenoble, point to "the largest entanglement depth reported so far in any quantum material," ac...

recommendations: Before merging, the human reviewer should write a corrections file at src/content/corrections/<YYYY-MM>/<article-slug>.json documenting the warning(s).
Consider adding trusted domains to config/source_allowlist.txt

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know), 677 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Neutral, non-sensational tone throughout; no editorializing, no AI self-reference. The technical explanation of quantum Fisher information, the strange-metal phenomenon, and the experimental setup is accurate and appropriately hedged ('may be the deepest,' 'point to') rather than overclaiming.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 6 sources were read from the locally saved, hash-verified gzip snapshots in sources/2026-07/tu-wien-physicists-detect-record-deep-quantum-entanglement-in-a-centimeter-sized-strange-metal-crystal/ — no live WebFetch was used for any source, since none of the 6 snapshots failed to save (manifest shows status_code 200 for all, file present for all, no null/error entries). Recomputed sha256 of each decompressed file and confirmed an exact match against manifest.json for all 6 entries before reading. Findings per source: (1) source-0.html.gz (ill.eu, sha256 7c797841...) — CONFIRMS the 'largest entanglement depth reported so far in any quantum material' quote, the Ce3Pd20Si6 formula, ThALES cold-neutron triple-axis spectrometer, 60 millikelvin / 1.73 tesla conditions, the Mazza quote ('In a normal material, one would expect a neutron to transfer its energy to an individual particle'), and 'groups of at least nine quantum-entangled entities act collectively.' Does NOT independently contain the 'Kondo destruction' / 'Landau order parameter' phrase (that phrase is confirmed instead via source-5, the dual-cited arXiv abstract). (2) source-1.html.gz (physicsworld.com, sha256 21aee288...) — CONFIRMS the Ce3Pd20Si6 formula, the 'parent' state of high-temperature superconductivity framing, and the Bühler-Paschen quote ('We had suspected that some of the intriguing properties of this state might be related to entanglement but were not able to pin it down until now') verbatim. Does NOT confirm the quote attributed to it in the article ('quantifies how sensitively a quantum system responds to a change') — Physics World's own text paraphrases this without quotation marks. (3) source-2.html.gz (phys.org, sha256 888f5aaa..., archive_fallback true — original returned 200 per manifest, Archive.org snapshot used per script policy, treated as canonical) — CONFIRMS the Mazza quote, the cerium/palladium/silicon crystal description, Peter Zoller's theoretical-framework attribution, Fakher Assaad (University of Würzburg) as lead theorist, and — importantly — IS the actual verbatim source of the 'quantifies how sensitively a quantum system responds to a change' quote, attributed on this page to Silke Bühler-Paschen, not to Physics World. Does NOT contain '0.07 meV' or 'energy resolution' figures the article also cites to this outlet. (4) source-3.html.gz (sciencedaily.com, sha256 d7de00c6...) — CONFIRMS the crystal being 'large enough to fit comfortably in the palm of your hand' and the Assaad/Würzburg attribution. (5) source-4.html.gz (thequantuminsider.com, sha256 7127ec8a...) — CONFIRMS Zoller's theoretical framework and Assaad/Würzburg as lead theorist; also contains the same phys.org-style QFI quote attributed to Bühler-Paschen (not Physics World), corroborating finding #3. Does not itself use the phrase 'Nature Physics' but the publication venue is independently confirmed by ILL and arXiv. (6) source-5.html.gz (arxiv.org/abs/2403.12779, sha256 658ae3be...) — this is the arXiv ABSTRACT page only (4,702 characters of extracted text: title, author list, abstract, submission history, no full-text body). CONFIRMS the paper title 'Quantum Fisher information in a strange metal,' the full 8-author list matching the article's author list, the Nature Physics 2026 journal reference, and — verbatim — both the 'Kondo destruction quantum critical point...strange metallicity is associated with fluctuations beyond a Landau order parameter' quote and the 'opens a new direction for studies across strange metal platforms' quote used in the article's closing section. Does NOT contain '0.07 meV,' the QFI value '8.2,' or the phrase 'very most conservative estimate' — these figures, solely or jointly cited to this URL, are not present in the captured snapshot of that URL (see Findings). No source needed a live-WebFetch fallback; all snapshots were readable and none had failed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline, summary, and Overview lead are all solidly corroborated by at least two independent snapshots each ('at least nine' entangled entities/particles appears verbatim or near-verbatim in 4 of 6 sources; 'largest/deepest entanglement depth reported so far' is a direct quote confirmed in the ILL snapshot). Two subordinate body-paragraph specifics (the 0.07 meV energy-resolution figure, and the QFI=8.2 / 'very most conservative estimate' figure) are not verifiable from the snapshot content actually captured for the cited URLs — flagged as findings, not treated as fabrication, since the underlying paper is real and paywalled/full-text-not-captured, not evidence the numbers are invented. One quote is verbatim-real but cited to the wrong outlet (Physics World instead of phys.org/Bühler-Paschen).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Appropriately hedges the significance of the finding and includes a substantive 'What We Don't Know' section noting the result is limited to one compound and one quantum critical point, which is good practice for a physics News piece.
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/ for overlapping coverage. No existing article covers this TU Wien / ILL / Nature Physics study, quantum Fisher information, or this specific strange-metal entanglement finding. Two topically-adjacent prior articles exist but are clearly distinct: src/content/articles/2026-05/21-rice-and-weizmann-physicists-identify-the-electronic-agents-behind-strange-metallicity-in-a-flat-band-kagome-metal.md (different institution, different material — Ni3In flat-band kagome metal vs. Ce3Pd20Si6 heavy-fermion crystal, different technique — atomic-resolution STM spectroscopy vs. inelastic neutron scattering, different finding — microscopic orbital origin of strange metallicity vs. entanglement-depth measurement; note Qimiao Si is a co-author on both underlying papers but the studies are unrelated in method and result) and src/content/articles/2026-02/24-cisco-and-qunnect-demonstrate-first-metro-scale-quantum-entanglement-network-across-new-york-city.md (metro-scale fiber-optic entanglement networking/telecom infrastructure, unrelated subject matter beyond the shared word 'entanglement'). Also checked the two other quantum-adjacent submissions under parallel review: PR #2006 (Shanghai startup Zhongqi Wuliang's server-rack neutral-atom quantum computer, hardware/computing) and PR #2011 (Quantinuum's universal topological gate set via non-Abelian anyons, quantum computing gates). Both are quantum-computing hardware stories from commercial/research-lab quantum computing efforts; this submission is condensed-matter physics (a naturally occurring strange-metal material's entanglement properties, measured via neutron scattering at a European large-scale facility) — a genuinely distinct field, institution set, and angle from both. No duplication risk identified.
concerns: A direct quote ('quantifies how sensitively a quantum system responds to a change') is attributed to Physics World but is actually verbatim content from phys.org, spoken by Silke Bühler-Paschen — the citation names the wrong outlet and drops the speaker attribution.

Two specific numeric/quote details in the body (energy resolution of ~0.07 meV; QFI witness value of 8.2 and the phrase 'the very most conservative estimate') are cited to sources whose captured snapshots (the phys.org article and the arXiv abstract page) do not contain them — the arXiv citation in particular points to the abstract-only page rather than the full text where such figures would appear.

Two of the six sources (ill.eu, physicsworld.com) are not yet in config/source_allowlist.txt, though both are unquestionably reputable (a major European neutron-science research facility and an IOP Publishing science-journalism outlet).
recommendations: File a corrections record for the two content issues (quote misattribution; unverified specific figures) per APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS workflow.
Add ill.eu and physicsworld.com to config/source_allowlist.txt as trusted science/research domains.
For future submissions citing arXiv, prefer citing (and snapshotting) the full-text HTML/PDF view rather than the /abs/ metadata page when specific in-paper figures are being sourced.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced News piece on a genuine, newly published (Nature Physics, 2026) physics result. Headline, summary, and lead are solidly corroborated across independent sources. Two recoverable issues in supporting body paragraphs — a real quote attributed to the wrong outlet, and two specific technical figures not present in the captured snapshot content for their cited sources — are each honestly summarizable in a public corrections note and do not undermine the article's central, well-supported thesis. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
